CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zuyaml parses and emits YAML 1.2 to and from ordinary R objects through a vendored copy of the cyaml C11 library, with no system library and no runtime dependency beyond R. It is strict where YAML is ambiguous: duplicate keys are refused by default, the 1.2 core schema means yes and no are strings, integers beyond 2^53 are kept as zuyaml_bigint, and a stream (_all) is kept apart from a sequence. max_size, max_depth and max_nodes bound untrusted input, max_nodes being what stops alias bombs. The C layer uses the R C API directly: no Rcpp, cpp11 or C++. A persistent document API is future work (design §20), and no performance claim belongs in user-facing text.

Three documents in .agents/ are the specification and outrank this file: DESIGN-zuyaml.md (what to build; key decisions §21, open questions §22), ROADMAP.md (milestones M0–M9) and STATUS.md (what was demonstrated, and what upstream actually does). The design’s verification note applies to every cyaml claim: grep the implementation and write a test, because the header and README are not reliable.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11. 0.1.0 is on CRAN (published 2026-10-07) with the API complete but explicitly not frozen. main is 0.1.0.9000 with no changes yet in NEWS.md. Milestones M0–M6.6 are done. M7 (freeze to 1.0.0) waits on the three open questions in design §22 (key stringification, eight versus five functions, whether zuyaml_bigint and zuyaml_map belong in 1.0) and on conditionCall(), which is still NULL in both layers (R/conditions.R, src/zuyaml_error.c). STATUS.md was last revised 2026-09-14, before the release, so its release and housekeeping notes are out of date.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #15 for v0.1.1; its one sub-issue is #14, adopting zufast for scalar number resolution. #17 is the reminder that the next submission opens from 2026-11-18. Sibling packages that depend on this one: none yet. Design §19 plans zuhttp’s use of it for YAML response bodies.

Commands

Occasional, from the package root:

tools/vendor-cyaml.sh                          # re-vendor cyaml at the pinned commit
tools/fetch-yaml-test-suite.sh <dir>           # check out the full upstream suite
Rscript tools/conformance.R <dir>              # full suite vs the pinned baseline
Rscript tools/curate-test-suite.R <dir>        # rebuild the shipped subset
Rscript tools/sanitizer-exercise.R <fixtures>  # base-R driver for ASan
Rscript tools/benchmark.R                      # against the yaml package

Before a sanitizer or benchmark build, find src -name '*.o' -delete: load_all() leaves -O0 objects in src/, and R CMD INSTALL . reuses any .o newer than its .c, so the build is silently uninstrumented or unoptimised. nm -u .../zuyaml.so | grep -c asan tells an instrumented build from one that is not.

Architecture

  • Vendored cyaml lives flat in src/ (cyaml*.c, cyaml*.h), not in src/vendor/, because R CMD SHLIB compiles only top-level sources and a subdirectory would need a hand-kept OBJECTS list in both Makevars files. zuyaml_-prefixed files are ours. All eight .c files are vendored, including the unused YPATH, JSON, modify and events units, because cyaml.c references them (design §13.1).
  • Two entry points (design §9.2): zuyaml_parse_() always returns a list of documents, and yaml_parse() is an R wrapper that requires exactly one; zuyaml_emit_() emits. Argument validation (types, ranges, match.arg()) happens in R; C trusts what it receives.
  • src/zuyaml_convert.c turns the cyaml tree into R values (design §6, §9.5), src/zuyaml_emit.c builds a cyaml document from R values and picks scalar styles (§7), src/zuyaml_error.c maps cyaml_err_t to the stable code strings of §10.1, and src/zuyaml_panic.c is where patch 0001 sends cyaml’s assertions.
  • src/init.c registers both entry points with R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE) and R_forceSymbols(dll, TRUE).
  • Errors are zuyaml_parse_error (and siblings) inheriting zuyaml_error, carrying code, line, column, end_line, end_column and, for files, path. The message is composed by zuyaml, never passed through from cyaml.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • A parsed cyaml stream is owned by a transient external pointer with a finalizer, from the moment cyaml_parse_stream() succeeds. Any Rf_error(), allocation failure or interrupt would otherwise unwind past cyaml_stream_free() and leak the tree. The same holds for the emit path’s cyaml_doc_t and output buffer (design §9.3).
  • The char * from cyaml_scalar_str() must not be live across an allocating R call. Plain scalars take the zero-copy path through cyaml_str()/cyaml_len() instead (design §9.5).
  • The parsed tree borrows its source buffer: keep the input SEXP protected for the whole call (design §9.4).
  • Rf_getAttrib() can allocate: protect its result before passing it on. rchk found exactly this in build_node(), which nothing else caught.
  • cyaml ignores dup_keys, max_depth and max_size and never raises CYAML_ERR_DUP_KEY. zuyaml enforces all three itself; do not hand them to cyaml and assume they work.
  • Scan for NUL before parsing and during conversion, and skip a leading BOM: the parser treats a literal NUL as end of input and drops the rest silently, and leaves a BOM inside the first scalar.
  • Emitter round trip: the same “needs a non-plain style” predicate applies to values and keys, integral doubles emit as floats (1.0), and NULL and NA emit as an explicit null. Each rule closed a silent data loss found in M6.5.
  • Doubles are formatted by zuyaml, not by cyaml_new_float() (%g, six digits). An out-of-range float becomes the nearest double, never a string (out_of_range_double() in zuyaml_convert.c), so a field’s R type never depends on its magnitude.
  • A new upstream error code must fail loudly in the §10.1 mapping, not fall through to a default.
  • Never define CYAML_DEBUG or CYAML_TRACE: they enable printf() and stderr paths that CRAN rejects. CYAML_VERSION_STR must be set in both Makevars files, or cyaml_version() misreports and test-vendor.R fails.
  • No snapshot tests of message text: callers rely on code, line and column, and tests assert those.

Testing

  • Conformance: tests/testthat/fixtures/yaml-test-suite/ is a curated 84-case subset of the upstream yaml-test-suite, kept small for CRAN time; test-conformance.R checks valid versus invalid and test-conformance-semantic.R compares against the suite’s in.json. The full suite runs outside tests/ through tools/conformance.R, against a pinned baseline. The one deliberate semantic difference is case WZ62.
  • Round trip: every suite case that emits must reparse to the same value, plus generated strings and every one- and two-character string over the indicator alphabet (test-round-trip.R).
  • Unwind safety: test-unwind-safety.R runs poisoning loops over error paths and then asserts an ordinary parse still works, plus format-specifier and R_forceSymbols checks.
  • Helpers: helper-doubles.R builds doubles from IEEE-754 bit patterns (dbl()), because R’s reader is not correctly rounded on aarch64 and reads DBL_MAX written out in full as Inf. Write numeric expectations that way, never as R literals.
  • test-fuzz.R holds the fuzz cases; hardening.yaml runs them at larger iteration counts through tools/ci-run-tests.R fuzz.

Continuous integration

Shared r-actions workflows at @v1: R-CMD-check.yaml (with NOSUGGESTS, since the suite needs only two of five Suggests, and NOLD, since number parsing and emitting can be right only by accident of 80-bit intermediates), coverage.yaml, and native-checks.yaml: sanitizers (ASan driven by tools/sanitizer-exercise.R over the fixtures), valgrind, LTO, rchk, CRAN’s special flavours, and gctorture twice: step 500 on every push, step 20 weekly and on demand. rchk stays permanently, because it alone found the build_node() PROTECT bug.

Package-owned: hardening.yaml fetches the full yaml-test-suite and runs the suite, tools/conformance.R and the fuzz cases, weekly and on push. pkgdown.yaml builds the site.

Open CI gaps: #9 (no vendor.yml, so nothing guards hand edits to src/cyaml*.c) and #7 (-Wextra no longer runs anywhere).

Vendored native code

cyaml (andrewmd5/cyaml), MIT, tag v0.1.3, commit 0672e81b, vendored 2026-09-08. inst/cyaml-VERSION is the generated record; tools/vendor-cyaml.sh verifies each upstream file against its own SHA-256 manifest, because GitHub archives are not byte-stable. Five mandatory patches in tools/patches/, each explained in its README.md:

  • 0001 routes CYAML_ASSERT and CYAML_UNREACHABLE to zuyaml_panic() instead of fprintf(stderr) and abort(). It leaks on that path, which is acceptable only because it fires on a cyaml bug.
  • 0002 stops the emitter promoting plain null/true/false/~ to double-quoted, so logicals emit as booleans.
  • 0003 fixes appending a zero-length document.
  • 0004 fixes cyaml_str_to_i64() at INT64_MIN.
  • 0005 makes cyaml_scalar_str() return a built node’s span verbatim, so emitted strings keep their line breaks.

Keep upstream recognisable: no reformatting or renaming, and every change as a patch. Four upstream bugs are recorded in STATUS.md but not yet reported.
